lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: asking a trusted adult for help

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 4: Body Signals, Rest, and Fueling Meals
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice asking a trusted adult for help. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Sometimes a learner notices hunger, thirst, stress, or being overly tired but doesn't say anything to a trusted adult, or asks in a way that's hard to act on, like saying they don't feel good.
materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l06-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l06-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l06-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u04-l06-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Write the specific two-part request (signal plus need) you plan to actually use next time you notice hunger, thirst, stress, or tiredness, and explain why you chose that wording.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u04-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Request specificity: The specific version names the actual signal and one clear, actionable need. | Predictive reasoning: The learner predicts a plausible difference in response and names one reason the specific version is easier to act on. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner practice saying their specific two-part request out loud to a trusted adult in a calm moment, not during an actual signal, and write down what the adult said back.

resources.title: asking a trusted adult for help worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Sometimes a learner notices hunger, thirst, stress, or being overly tired but doesn't say anything to a trusted adult, or asks in a way that's hard to act on, like saying they don't feel good.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact asking a trusted adult for help decision or action.

Model move 2: Think back over the last week to one specific moment when you noticed a body signal (hunger, thirst, stress, or tiredness) but didn't ask a trusted adult for help with it, or asked in a way that was hard to understand.

Model move 3: For that same moment, write two versions of what you could have said: a vague version, like saying you don't feel good, and a specific version that names both the signal and what you need, like naming that your stomach feels empty and asking for something to eat soon.

Model check: Request specificity: The specific version names the actual signal and one clear, actionable need. | Predictive reasoning: The learner predicts a plausible difference in response and names one reason the specific version is easier to act on.

resources.title: asking a trusted adult for help coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Sometimes a learner notices hunger, thirst, stress, or being overly tired but doesn't say anything to a trusted adult, or asks in a way that's hard to act on, like saying they don't feel good.

Coach direction: Think back over the last week to one specific moment when you noticed a body signal (hunger, thirst, stress, or tiredness) but didn't ask a trusted adult for help with it, or asked in a way that was hard to understand.
Learner prompt: Describe that moment: what signal did you notice, and what happened instead of asking clearly?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: asking a trusted adult for help complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: For that same moment, write two versions of what you could have said: a vague version, like saying you don't feel good, and a specific version that names both the signal and what you need, like naming that your stomach feels empty and asking for something to eat soon.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My vague version is realistic, close to something I might actually say without thinking.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My specific version names the actual signal I noticed.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My specific version names one clear thing I need, not just a description of the problem.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: asking a trusted adult for help minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Write the specific two-part request (signal plus need) you plan to actually use next time you notice hunger, thirst, stress, or tiredness, and explain why you chose that wording.

Success checks: Request specificity: The specific version names the actual signal and one clear, actionable need. | Predictive reasoning: The learner predicts a plausible difference in response and names one reason the specific version is easier to act on.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: asking a trusted adult for help supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u04-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional asking a trusted adult for help condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Request specificity: The specific version names the actual signal and one clear, actionable need. | Predictive reasoning: The learner predicts a plausible difference in response and names one reason the specific version is easier to act on..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u04-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.

safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.
